item.text:
**What changed.** The diff moves three redirect helpers from `httpx/_utils.py` into `httpx/_client.py` and gives them private names. Their logic is unchanged. Five existing tests move from `tests/test_utils.py` to `tests/client/test_headers.py` with identical assertions. [Client helpers](<work>/pr3389-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:61) · [Header tests](<work>/pr3389-rules-official-codex/tests/client/test_headers.py:240)

**Affected callers and behavior.** Both `Client` and `AsyncClient` use `BaseClient._build_redirect_request`, which calls `_redirect_headers`. Same-origin redirects preserve `Host` and `Authorization`. Cross-origin redirects rewrite `Host` and strip `Authorization`, except that same-host HTTP-to-HTTPS upgrades on the default ports retain `Authorization`. Existing end-to-end tests cover the authorization behavior. [Redirect handling](<work>/pr3389-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:545) · [Redirect tests](<work>/pr3389-rules-official-codex/tests/client/test_redirects.py:275)

**Risks.** No runtime regression is apparent from the diff. Downstream code that imports the removed names from `httpx._utils` will fail to import them. The repository search found no remaining internal callers of those names. The relocated `Host` tests also have a pre-existing blind spot: the source and destination normalize to the same `Host` value, so the assertions cannot distinguish preservation from rewriting. [Utilities](<work>/pr3389-rules-official-codex/httpx/_utils.py) · [Host assertions](<work>/pr3389-rules-official-codex/tests/client/test_headers.py:240)

`git diff --check` passed. The targeted tests could not run because `pytest` was unavailable in the local Python environment.
